newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: Malaysia rubber ends down in trading lull.
newsitem.headline: Malaysia rubber ends down in trading lull.

text.p: Malaysian rubber prices ended lower after a day-long lull in trading due to absence of consumer interest, traders said.
No buying or selling was reported for the day, traders said, adding that sentiment was not helped by uncertainties in the Tokyo futures market.
"The (local) market was very quiet," said a trader.

He said most overseas buyers seemed pre-occupied with the year-end holidays. Sellers, who usually worried about the effect of the weather on stocks, also reacted indifferently to reports of rain in domestic growing areas, he said.
At the close, the MRELB quoted January RSS1 buyer at 315.50 cents ($1.25) a kg, down half cent from Wednesday. January SMR 20 buyer was also 1.50 cents lower at 303.

Trading houses offered the SMR CV at 362 cents, SMR L at 341, SMR 5 at 316, SMR 10 at 305, SMR 20 at 304 and drum latex at 234. Traders said they expect business to be slow through December with most market players going on holiday.
The INRO five-day moving average fell to 241.67 Malaysian/Singapore cents per kg on Dec 4 from 242.16 on Dec 3. The daily indicator price dipped to 240.48 from 241.76.
